methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study of 109 early-stage EC patients stratified by BMI (Group A ≥40, Group B 30-39.9, Group C <30 kg/m²). Sample size calculation based on 19% vs 2% conversion rates achieves 80% power with n=100. Statistical methods appropriate: one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc testing for continuous variables; chi-square for categorical; odds ratios with 95% CIs for significant variables (p<0.05). However, retrospective design with unmeasured confounders (body fat distribution, functional status); single surgeon/limited surgeon experience; small Class III cohort (n=26); only 2 conversions in entire cohort limits statistical power for conversion comparison.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective comparative cohort study (LoE 3b) evaluating surgical feasibility and safety of robotic hysterectomy in Class III obese EC patients. Direct clinical relevance: addresses specific perioperative concerns in morbidly obese population at high lifetime EC risk (10-15%). Demonstrates that robotic approach remains safe despite increased operative time, relevant for surgical technique selection. However, findings specific to experienced centers; generalizability limited; outcomes measured at 3-month follow-up limit assessment of long-term oncologic adequacy.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE-compliant reporting with clear study design, participant selection criteria, and variable definitions. Methods comprehensively described including operative procedure, robotic technique, lymph node assessment algorithm, and Clavien-Dindo toxicity classification. Results systematically presented with baseline characteristics table and perioperative outcomes by group. However, no data availability statement provided; individual patient data or code not shared. STROBE framework explicitly referenced and followed.

novelty_literature.justification: Comparative analysis of robotic surgery outcomes across BMI categories; robotic surgery feasibility in obese patients previously reported in smaller series. Main findings (prolonged operative time, lower bilateral SLN mapping success in Class III group, comparable safety) represent confirmatory rather than novel observations. Incremental contribution: largest Class III EC cohort with BMI-stratified analysis; standardized protocols and structured follow-up; identifies specific operational challenges (SLN mapping) requiring optimization.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear motivation addressing understudied Class III obesity subgroup. Methods logically presented with rationale for BMI stratification and feasibility definition. Results systematically organized with baseline characteristics, conversion rates, operative metrics, and complication data. Discussion appropriately acknowledges strengths (well-characterized cohort, large Class III sample) and limitations (single-center retrospective design, unmeasured confounders, low overall complication rates limiting comparative statistical power). Future directions including RObese trial mentioned appropriately.

key_strengths: Large Class III obesity cohort (n=26) with homogeneous baseline characteristics supporting robust BMI comparison
Zero conversions in Class III group with low overall conversion rate (1.8%), demonstrating technical feasibility
Safety profile comparable across BMI groups with no difference in intraoperative/postoperative complication rates (p=0.805), ICU/hospital stay, or blood loss
Comprehensive follow-up with structured 30- and 90-day assessments; clear identification of SLN mapping challenges enabling targeted solutions
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design with potential selection bias; patients included likely reflect referral patterns and surgeon preferences rather than population-based cohort
Unmeasured confounders including body fat distribution, metabolic comorbidities, functional status, and patient selection criteria not fully detailed
Single or limited surgeon experience; results heavily dependent on operator expertise; generalizability to community centers with less robotic experience uncertain
Small absolute number of Class III patients (n=26); study not powered to detect true differences in rare complications; low event rates limit precision of estimates
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 comparative surgical study appropriate for gynecologic oncology journal. Addresses pragmatic question with adequate sample size and safety profile. Single-center and retrospective nature prevent higher tier. Results support robotic approach feasibility in Class III obese EC patients at experienced centers.
